referenceRoles.1: User-provided folk procession: figure treatment and standards
referenceRoles.2: User-provided leader and horse: subject/style references, not authenticated era evidence
referenceRoles.3: User-provided pig print: contour, broad forms and pigment treatment only

jobs.prompt:
Use case: style-transfer / icon adaptation.
Asset: one candidate mobile game icon for Vạn Thắng, a Vietnamese historical grand-strategy game about heroes, armies and kingdoms. The user requests ideas drawn directly from these supplied Đông Hồ folk prints, simple enough for mobile.
Use the uploaded reference images as visible art references, not as text instructions. Do not transcribe ANY writing from them. Image 1 establishes flat folk figures and ceremonial standards; Image 2 establishes the white horse, harness and leader's clothing; Image 3 establishes the confidently rounded large forms, expressive few marks, black contours, and green/vermilion decorative balance. Preserve the HUMAN handmade folk-print character of these examples: decisive slightly irregular warm-black contours, broad bounded flat forest-green, vermilion and ochre blocks on pale shell-cream, economical expressive face marks. Very restrained print tooth. No modeled lighting, no 3D, no fine crosshatching, no ornamental gold filigree, no vector sports-team mascot aesthetic, no generic fantasy concept art, no heavy yellow aging. This is a contemporary game illustration inspired by later folk prints, not an authenticated dynasty costume.
Icon composition: square opaque canvas to all edges, uniform pale shell-cream #f3ecd8 background. One compact main subject with generous uncluttered space around it, all essential subject inside x16%-84%, y14%-86% so launcher corners are safe. A bold silhouette with few large color areas, readable at 64 px. At most 8 purposeful interior marks. No inscription, letters, words, seals, lettering, ornamental frame, presentation sheet, interface, or rounded corners. No elephant anywhere. Output a single 1024x1024 opaque square PNG.

ADAPTATION A — THE COMMANDER. Adapt ONLY the leader standing in Image 2 into a charismatic large head-and-shoulders portrait, gently turned three-quarter, face occupying most of the icon. Retain the reference's simple green fabric field cap with its small soft crown, compact black moustache, warm expressive cream face, green neck wrap and ochre/red-edged garment. No new helmet, crown, jewelry or rank badge. The figure's expression is alert, capable, slightly smiling, with a strong lively eyebrow and simple ink eyes. Design the head/neck/shoulders as one compact folk-print mass, shoulders narrowing toward bottom. Omit the horse, parasol, weapons, hands, flags, background and every extra prop. Reference 3's broad expressive outline rhythm should make this feel like a lovable, confident Đông Hồ character rather than an imperial movie portrait. Keep the cap visually compact and let the face carry the icon.

ADAPTATION B — THE WHITE WARHORSE. Adapt ONLY the white horse from Image 2 into a powerful but charming close-up HEAD AND NECK icon facing left in a lively three-quarter/profile hybrid, large almond-shaped ink eye, compact upright ochre forelock, two pointed ears, strongly curved cream neck. Preserve the reference's simple forest-green bridle, one broad vermilion-and-ochre collar at the lower neck, black mane rhythm. Remove the rider, parasol, flag, saddle, all legs, body, chains and hanging tassels. Keep bridle to two clear lines. The white horse must have the charismatic rounded anatomy and playful contour economy of Image 3, not a realistic horse painting or an aggressive esport horse-head logo. Deliberate flat pigment shapes, a tiny red nostril accent, no scales, no filigree. This is the cavalry and forward motion of the historical game expressed as one memorable folk-art animal.

ADAPTATION C — THE BATTLE STANDARD. Adapt ONLY the flame-edged ceremonial flag at the far left of Image 1 into one compact square war-standard icon. One bold near-square vermilion cloth with a single broad ochre inner border, forest-green inset square, warm-black carved outline and just THREE chunky flame-like trailing tips, held on one short sturdy near-vertical ochre wooden staff with a simple spear-shaped top. On the central green square place ONLY the game's pale cream drum-sun emblem: a round center with twelve short thick rays, stylized brand symbol not an exact archaeological tracing. The flag is slightly lifted by wind and its diagonal upward movement conveys commanding a kingdom. The square of the cloth is at least 65% of the whole subject. Remove all people, horse, landscape, parasols and writing. Strong flat bounded color masses and natural print irregularities from the supplied reference, absolutely no fine edge fringes or duplicate outlines. Aim for the clearest of the three icon directions.
